channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Indian Prime Minister arrives in Uzbekistan for state visit
item.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi arrived in Uzbekistan for a state visit at the invitation of President Shavkat Mirziyoyev. He was welcomed at Tashkent-Humo International Airport by the Uzbek President. State flags and an honor guard were present for the occasion.

item.title: Chinese magazine features Uzbekistan's 35th independence anniversary
item.description: A special issue of China's 'Luokai' magazine highlights Uzbekistan's 35th independence anniversary, detailing reforms and achievements in politics, economy, and culture. It covers bilateral cooperation, investment potential, the Islamic Civilization Center, and the 'Uzbekistan-2030' strategy.

item.title: Uzbekistan and India's Strategic Partnership Shows Growing Momentum
item.description: Uzbek-Indian relations have gained new momentum since 2017, evolving beyond political dialogue to multifaceted practical cooperation. This strategic partnership spans politics, economy, industry, health, digital sectors, education, security, and transport, driven by political will and complementary economies.

item.title: Russia's Foreign Ministry Calls Armenia's Mobilization Statements a Provocation
item.description: Russia's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova labeled statements by Armenian Security Council Secretary Alen Simonyan regarding accepting Russians in case of mobilization as a provocation. Zakharova stated Simonyan's remarks encourage illegal actions and politicize Armenian hospitality. The ministry expressed regret over Yerevan's public statements undermining bilateral cooperation with Moscow.

item.title: Uzbekistan Presents Parliamentary Diplomacy Experience at Phnom Penh Conference
item.description: Uzbekistan shared its parliamentary diplomacy experience at the II Inter-Parliamentary Conference in Phnom Penh, Cambodia. The delegation highlighted the strengthening atmosphere of good neighborliness and cooperation in Central Asia, emphasizing constructive dialogue for conflict resolution.

item.title: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi Arrives in Uzbekistan for State Visit
item.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi arrived in Uzbekistan on Saturday for a state visit, where he was welcomed by President Shavkat Mirziyoyev at the Tashkent airport. Key events are scheduled for Sunday, including discussions on trade, investment, defense, energy, and education. Agreements are expected to be signed.

item.title: Uzbekistan's startups to gain new opportunities for international market entry
item.description: Uzbekistan's Minister of Digital Technologies met with 500 Global's managing partner to discuss developing the startup ecosystem, increasing venture investments, and facilitating international market access for local startups. The company expressed interest in programs to prepare Uzbek startups for global investment markets and expand their interaction with foreign investors.

item.title: New AIDS center opens in Namangan, enhancing medical care quality
item.description: A new building for the AIDS Center has been commissioned in Namangan region, Uzbekistan. Equipped with modern diagnostic laboratories and patient care facilities, it aims to expand HIV testing, improve patient care, and ensure timely medication. The project, costing over $1.25 million, significantly increases the lab's capacity to 10,000 tests daily.

item.title: Nearly 400 Trucks Congested at Kazakhstan-Kyrgyzstan Border Crossing
item.description: Approximately 400 trucks are backed up at the Karasu border crossing in Kazakhstan's Zhambyl region, heading towards Kyrgyzstan. The congestion is attributed to a seasonal increase in freight transport and temperature restrictions on truck movement in Kyrgyzstan. Border services are working to manage the flow.

item.title: China plans to deepen cooperation with Kyrgyzstan in multiple sectors
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping outlined plans to expand cooperation with Kyrgyzstan in trade, investment, infrastructure, green minerals, digital economy, clean energy, and AI. He expressed anticipation for jointly developing a new plan for China-Kyrgyzstan relations and noted the countries' evolution to a comprehensive strategic partnership.

item.title: China Aims to Expand Cooperation with Kyrgyzstan in Key Sectors, Says Xi Jinping
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping expressed China's intention to expand cooperation with Kyrgyzstan in trade, investment, infrastructure, green minerals, digital economy, clean energy, and artificial intelligence. He highlighted the strategic partnership and the 'community with a shared future' between the two nations.

item.title: Danish policy of forced contraception in Greenland violated women's rights
item.description: Two independent studies concluded that Denmark's forced contraception policy in Greenland violated women's rights, though experts differed on the scale and systematic nature of the violations. The investigations found that contraception was applied without valid consent, violating women's rights to privacy and family life, and in some cases was degrading.

item.title: China and Kyrgyzstan should always be each other's support, says Xi Jinping
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping stated that China and Kyrgyzstan should be pillars of each other's development. He emphasized strengthening good-neighborliness, maintaining high-level contacts, and aligning development strategies. Xi also expressed China's willingness to assist Kyrgyzstan's economic development and improve its people's well-being.

item.title: Stone Artifacts Found at Arkutsoy Site May Date Back 320-280 Thousand Years
item.description: Stone tools potentially dating back 320-280 thousand years have been discovered at the Arkutsoy Paleolithic site in Uzbekistan's Tashkent region. If confirmed by lab analysis, Arkutsoy could be recognized as the oldest known archaeological site in Uzbekistan, according to the Academy of Sciences.

item.title: China and Kyrgyzstan Should Be Pillars of Support for Each Other, Says Xi Jinping
item.description: In an article ahead of his state visit, Chinese President Xi Jinping stated that China and Kyrgyzstan should be pillars of development support for each other. He emphasized strengthening good-neighborliness, maintaining high-level contacts, and deepening cooperation in governance, culture, tourism, and media.

item.title: China and Kyrgyzstan should always be each other's support, says Xi Jinping
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping stated that China and Kyrgyzstan should be pillars of each other's development. He emphasized strengthening good-neighborliness, maintaining high-level contacts, and aligning development strategies. Xi also expressed China's willingness to assist Kyrgyzstan's economic development and improve its people's well-being.

item.title: Xi Jinping plans new development strategy for China-Kyrgyzstan relations
item.description: Ahead of his state visit, Chinese President Xi Jinping published an article outlining a vision for bilateral relations, emphasizing economic cooperation. He noted China's role as Kyrgyzstan's largest trade partner and investor, highlighting joint projects like the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway and improved transport links.

item.title: Uzbekistan collected over 3 trillion soms for IMEI codes in seven years
item.description: Uzbekistan has collected over 3 trillion soms for mobile device IMEI code registration in the past seven years. The UzIMEI system operator stated these payments are not taxes but service fees. The system aims to encourage official imports and the opening of authorized stores.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Aims to Launch 75 New Agricultural Processing Enterprises by End of 2026
item.description: Kyrgyzstan plans to launch 75 new agricultural processing and production facilities by the end of 2026, according to the Ministry of Agriculture. This initiative aims to increase the number of new enterprises by nearly 19% compared to 2025, focusing on processing milk, meat, fruits, vegetables, and fish, as well as food production and logistics across all regions.

item.title: Kazakhstan establishes new state body directly accountable to the president
item.description: Kazakhstan has established a new state body, the Security Council Apparatus, which is directly subordinate to and accountable to the President. President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev signed a decree on August 29 to further improve the state management system.

item.title: Kyrgyz Pochtasy and Chinese firm to launch e-commerce platform in Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Kyrgyz Pochtasy OJSC and China's Kashgar Fengxin Trading Co., Ltd. will develop an e-commerce platform in Kyrgyzstan to boost trade and digital solutions. The platform will integrate e-commerce with postal logistics, offering nationwide delivery and new market opportunities for Kyrgyz businesses. It will also incorporate AI technologies for digital content and services.

item.title: SCO Summit to convene in Bishkek on September 1 with heads of state attending
item.description: Kyrgyzstan will host the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Council of Heads of State meeting and an SCO Plus high-level meeting on September 1 in Bishkek. President Sadyr Japarov will chair the event, which will be attended by leaders from Belarus, India, Iran, Kazakhstan, China, Pakistan, Russia, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, and other nations.

item.title: World Nomad Games Evolve from Local Tournament to Global Movement
item.description: The World Nomad Games, originating in Kyrgyzstan, have grown from a small tournament with 19 countries into a major international event promoting ethnosport, culture, and research. The games are set to return to Kyrgyzstan in 2026. The initiative, launched in 2012, aims to preserve nomadic heritage and was recognized by UNESCO for its efforts.

item.title: Uzbekistan Introduces "Presumption of Legality" for Entrepreneurs
item.description: Uzbekistan will implement a "presumption of legality" in relations between state bodies and entrepreneurs. Under the new rule, entrepreneurs are considered to have acted lawfully and fulfilled their obligations unless the state proves otherwise. The burden of proof for the legality and proportionality of state actions will fall on the state.

item.title: Kyrgyz Post and Chinese Firm to Launch E-commerce Platform
item.description: Kyrgyz Post and China's Kashgar Fengxin Trading Co., Ltd. have agreed to collaborate on developing an e-commerce platform in Kyrgyzstan. The project aims to boost trade, integrate logistics, and provide Kyrgyz entrepreneurs with new market access. It will also incorporate digital content and AI services, transforming postal infrastructure into a digital ecosystem.

item.title: UN: Annual $278 Billion Funding Gap for Land Restoration
item.description: The UN reports that $355 billion is needed annually for global land restoration by 2030, but current investments total only $77 billion, leaving a $278 billion deficit. Private funding accounts for only six percent of global investments. A new initiative for rangelands and a $1.3 billion funding portfolio for 23 countries were announced at the COP17 conference.

item.title: Bishkek to host SCO summit with participation of numerous heads of state and international organizations
item.description: Bishkek will host the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit on September 1, chaired by Sadyr Japarov. Leaders from Belarus, India, Iran, Kazakhstan, China, Pakistan, Russia, Tajikistan, and Uzbekistan are expected to attend, alongside representatives from Azerbaijan, Armenia, Mongolia, Togo, Turkey, Laos, Vietnam, and Egypt. International organizations including the UN, CIS, CSTO, and others will also participate.

item.title: Uzbekistan Introduces Economic Amnesty for Small and Medium Businesses Until 2026
item.description: Uzbekistan has announced an economic amnesty for small and medium-sized businesses, valid until December 31, 2026. The initiative, named "Second Chance," aims to write off penalties on tax debts if the principal amount is paid by the deadline. It also allows businesses to correct past tax reporting errors without penalty.

item.title: Bodies of sisters found dead in UAE sent back to Kazakhstan
item.description: The bodies of sisters Akzhan and Zhuldyz Bokhanov, found dead in a Sharjah apartment, have been repatriated to Kazakhstan. The Consulate General of Kazakhstan in Dubai facilitated the return. The UAE authorities are investigating the circumstances of their deaths.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Calls for Strict Punishment of 'Enemies of the People'
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's President Sadyr Japarov demanded severe punishment for individuals allegedly receiving foreign funds to destabilize the country. Speaking at a security forces assembly, he stressed the importance of "iron discipline" and professionalism. A large-scale security operation involving 15,000 personnel is underway for upcoming international events.

item.title: Uzbekistan Imposes Three-Year Moratorium on Small Business Inspections
item.description: Uzbekistan will implement a three-year moratorium on inspections of small business entities. This measure, outlined in a presidential decree, aims to protect entrepreneurs. Exceptions apply to investigations related to criminal cases, human health, labor law compliance, citizen appeals, VAT refunds, and business liquidations.

item.title: India and Uzbekistan Expand Cooperation Across Multiple Sectors
item.description: India and Uzbekistan are deepening their strategic partnership, expanding cooperation beyond pharmaceuticals and trade into logistics, IT, energy, and defense. High-level visits and agreements, including around 20 documents signed during President Mirziyoyev's 2018 visit, have solidified bilateral ties. A virtual summit in 2020 further strengthened their robust partnership.

item.title: Third Kazakh Tourist Missing After Nepal Flood Disaster
item.description: A third Kazakh tourist is believed to be missing following a severe flood on the Nepal-China border. Kazakhstan's Foreign Ministry confirmed diplomatic efforts are underway with both countries to locate the missing citizens. The disaster, caused by a Himalayan glacier collapse, has claimed over 620 lives and left thousands missing.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev calls for nuclear powers to negotiate on eliminating weapons threat
item.description: On the International Day for Nuclear Test Ban, Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev urged nuclear powers to negotiate and sign the Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty. He highlighted Kazakhstan's voluntary renunciation of its nuclear arsenal and its commitment to global peace and security. Tokayev also noted public support for developing nuclear energy for peaceful purposes.

item.title: Uzbekistan Celebrates 35 Years of Independence with New Tashkent Inauguration
item.description: Uzbekistan marked its 35th anniversary of state independence with a ceremony in New Tashkent. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev congratulated the nation, highlighting the opening of new educational and cultural buildings. The event featured a Guinness World Record-holding fountain, symbolizing the nation's strength and development.

item.title: President Mirziyoyev Addresses Ceremony Marking Uzbekistan's 35 Years of Independence
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev addressed a ceremony celebrating Uzbekistan's 35th anniversary of independence, held in New Tashkent. He congratulated citizens and highlighted the opening of new university buildings and a Guinness World Record fountain. The president expressed confidence that New Tashkent will be a center of development.

item.title: Uzbekistan Ministry of Sports Holds Dialogue with 15,000 Coaches
item.description: Uzbekistan's Ministry of Sports hosted an unprecedented open dialogue with 15,000 coaches and specialists from across the country. Discussions covered the current state of sports, coach challenges, and proposals for future development. New initiatives include improving sports school management and streamlining athlete ranking processes.

item.title: Uzbekistan announces seven national programs for upcoming years
item.description: Uzbekistan will implement seven national programs covering education, healthcare, economy, ecology, rule of law, community development, and foreign policy in the coming years. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev announced these plans during the 35th anniversary of the country's independence. The programs aim to make knowledge and skills the "main capital" for future development and ensure all youth acquire a profession.

item.title: Indian Prime Minister to Visit Uzbekistan for State Visit
item.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi will visit Uzbekistan on August 29-30 at the invitation of President Shavkat Mirziyoyev. Discussions will focus on strengthening strategic partnership and cooperation in trade, energy, health, and other economic sectors. Bilateral agreements are expected to be signed.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Central Bank aims to increase local currency financing
item.description: Uzbekistan aims to gradually increase local currency financing and focus more on direct foreign investment rather than external debt, according to Central Bank Chairman Timur Ishmetov. This shift aims to mitigate currency risks historically associated with foreign currency borrowing. The market for soum-denominated financing is developing, with companies now issuing Eurobonds in national currency.
